instruction: I need to add the directory /usr/local/bin to my PATH environment variable permanently. Could you help me configure my shell so that this directory is included in PATH every time I open a terminal?

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding /usr/local/bin to PATH in .bashrc file. Evaluator checks if PATH export line with /usr/local/bin exists in .bashrc. Similar to the original - modifying shell configuration files for environment setup.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks for PATH modifications containing /usr/local/bin in ~/.bashrc
Grep pattern '(export[[:space:]]+)?PATH="?.*/usr/local/bin(:|"|\'|[[:space:]])' should match standard PATH modification patterns
Pattern matches both prepend (PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH") and append (PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/bin") formats
The optional 'export' prefix and proper delimiters (colon, quotes, whitespace) are correctly handled
Command logic '&& echo 1 || echo 0' correctly returns '1\n' on success and '0\n' on failure
Minor limitation: Only checks ~/.bashrc, might miss other valid shell config files like ~/.bash_profile or ~/.profile
Minor limitation: Pattern doesn't validate shell syntax correctness, only pattern presence
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking multiple shell config files to be more comprehensive: for f in ~/.bashrc ~/.bash_profile ~/.profile; do grep -E '...' $f && echo 1 && exit; done; echo 0
Optionally, verify the actual runtime PATH value after sourcing: bash -c 'source ~/.bashrc && echo $PATH' | grep -q '/usr/local/bin' && echo 1 || echo 0
